A central metric is interpreted inconsistently. Theorem 4.1/C.1 is not established under the stated assumptions. In the noiseless case, its right-hand side vanishes for zero observed labels, although no assumption excludes positive prediction error on unobserved inputs. The proof unjustifiably substitutes empirical kernel expressions for population bias and variance. The claimed O(1/n) rate also does not follow when effective dimension grows with sample size. Moreover, reducing effective dimension can increase bias, and the fixed-router analysis does not demonstrate the proposed evolving-routing mechanism.

Reproducibility and practical claims remain unsupported. Memorization thresholds, the cumulative routing-weight threshold, retained cohort sizes, and detailed evaluation settings are missing. Repeated inference on historical training samples and pairwise edit-distance calculations incur additional computation, so the claimed zero-cost monitoring requires overhead measurements.
